question: Which of the following species is also called the 'Kashmir Deer'?
solution:
**The correct answer is ‘Hangul’**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hangul (Kashmir Deer):**

 
 
• Hangul, also known as the **Kashmir Deer**, is the state animal of Jammu & Kashmir.
 
• It is primarily found in the **Dachigam National Park**, located near Srinagar.
 
• The species is listed as **Critically Endangered** on the IUCN Red List due to rapidly declining populations.
 
• It is protected under **Schedule I** of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, which ensures the highest degree of protection.
 
• Its population has drastically declined over decades due to habitat loss, poaching, and human interference.
 
• **Ex-situ conservation** efforts are being carried out in the forested areas of **Shikargah Tral** in South Kashmir.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Barasingha:**

 
 
• Also called the **Swamp Deer**, known for its distinctive multi-tined antlers.
 
• Mainly found in **Kanha National Park** of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It prefers swampy grasslands, unlike Hangul which is a mountain species.
 
 
 
• **Sangai:**
 
 
• Also known as the **Dancing Deer**, found in the floating biomass (phumdis) of **Keibul Lamjao National Park** in Manipur.
 
• It is one of the rarest deer species in the world and has a unique gait due to its wetland habitat.
 
 
 
• **Cheetal:**
 
 
• Commonly known as the **Spotted Deer** or **Axis Deer**.
 
• Widespread across the Indian subcontinent and commonly seen in many national parks.
 
• Unlike Hangul, it is not an endangered species and has a stable population.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• The Hangul population, once estimated at over 5,000 in the early 1900s, has fallen to **less than 200** today.
 
• Major threats include **habitat fragmentation, livestock grazing, poaching,** and political disturbances in the region.
 
• Conservation programs like the **Project Hangul** aim to restore and protect the species.
